title: Silas and the Wreck
premise: Casper Ravensworth, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries after a disaster he didn't cause, takes a quiet job ferrying supplies along a remote river valley. When a government survey team vanishes leaving gear but no tracks, Casper is the only one close enough to search—and what he finds implicates the same officials who ruined him. With monsoon season closing in, a leaking boat, and an orphaned river girl named Silas who knows every hidden channel, Casper must smuggle evidence of the cover-up downstream while evading men who want the truth drowned. The story ends with Casper surrendering himself to save Silas and the evidence, trusting a found family of river people to carry justice the rest of the way—and discovering that being seen was the thing that finally set him free.
about_author: Isandro Okonkwo is a former river-boat mechanic who spent a decade working seasonal routes through three continents before turning to fiction. He writes adventure stories about people the maps forgot, drawing on his own years of living off-season in towns too small to appear on them.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper ferries survey supplies upriver, counting distance to keep grief at bay, and establishes his careful invisibility after the blacklistings. When he learns a survey team has gone missing upstream, his instinct is to paddle away—but the gear left behind includes a radio still transmitting. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by obligation.

chapters.title: The Empty Camp
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Casper finds the abandoned camp: meals half-eaten, boots paired neatly, no tracks leading out. A torn map marks a tributary no official chart acknowledges. He realizes someone wanted the team found—or didn't want them found at all. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve as he decides to follow the unmarked water.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the Water
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Introduce Silas, a sharp-eyed river kid who survives by knowing channels adults ignore, watching Casper's boat from the reeds. Silas warns him the tributary floods first when the monsoon comes and offers passage for food. Emotional beat: two wary survivors testing whether trust is worth the risk.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Navigating the hidden tributary with Silas, they find the survey team's lead case—sealed field notes describing illegal dredging operations signed off by officials. One team member's journal reveals they were silenced, not lost. Emotional beat: Casper recognizes the machinery that destroyed him, now aimed at others.

chapters.title: Blacklisted Man's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Casper, flashback-woven. Casper weighs delivering the notes against burning them; the last time he told the truth, two countries erased him. Silas, blunt and unsentimental, asks why he'd protect men who'd let a kid drown. Emotional beat: the old wound reopened, and the first honest answer he's given in five years.

chapters.title: First Rain
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The monsoon arrives early. They shelter in a flooded church where Silas reveals her parents were river workers who died in a 'survey accident'—the same operation. Casper sees the pattern spans years. Emotional beat: shared grief becoming shared purpose; the found family begins.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Their patched boat starts taking water faster than it can be bailed. They limp to a stilt village where Aunt Verity, a matriarch who remembers Casper's father, offers repairs—and news: government boats are searching the tributary, asking about a guide. Emotional beat: sanctuary shadowed by pursuit.

chapters.title: Verity's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Verity keeps her own records—decades of payments, threats, and disappearances tied to the dredging cartel. She refuses to hand them over but teaches Casper how the network moves its money downriver. Emotional beat: Casper learns he was never alone in knowing; the silence was organized.

chapters.title: Men in Clean Boots
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Government agents reach the village, polite and menacing, offering Casper amnesty if he surrenders 'recovered property.' He lies well enough to buy a day, but they leave a watcher behind. Emotional beat: the temptation of going legitimate versus the knowledge that amnesty means a grave.

chapters.title: Night Channels
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas leads them out through flooded forest paths only she can read, losing the watcher in the dark. A near-drowning forces Casper to choose saving the notes or saving Silas without hesitation—he saves Silas. Emotional beat: proof, unspoken, that she matters more than the mission.

chapters.title: The Dredge at Kettle Bend
chapters.summary: POV Casper. They scout the illegal dredging site and find the missing survey team—not all dead. One survivor, Engineer Amara Osei, is held in a work camp, alive because she agreed to falsify reports. Emotional beat: horror tempered by hope; there is a witness worth everything.

chapters.title: Amara's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV Amara (first shift). Amara, kept compliant by threats against her family, secretly passes Casper the original sealed samples proving contamination. She won't run—yet—but agrees to testify if her family is protected. Emotional beat: complicity and courage wrestling in one exhausted woman.

chapters.title: Downstream Is a Trap
chapters.summary: POV Casper. The only route to authorities runs past checkpoint towns controlled by the cartel. Verity's network proposes moving the evidence by funeral barge—hidden in a coffin, in plain sight. Emotional beat: grim humor and solidarity; justice traveling disguised as mourning.

chapters.title: The Funeral Barge
chapters.summary: POV Silas. The barge journey: mourners who aren't mourning, a coffin full of documents, checkpoints passed by ritual and nerve. At the second checkpoint a young officer almost finds the cache until Silas performs grief so convincingly he backs away. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into fierce pride.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Halfway Lock
chapters.summary: POV Casper. A village ally sells their route to the cartel for his son's medical debt. Agents board at Halfway Lock; Casper scuttles the barge's cargo into a sunken cache only Silas can relocate, then lets himself be taken to draw pursuit. Emotional beat: sacrifice as strategy, and trust as a leap.

chapters.title: Interrogation in a Dry Room
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Held in a converted customs house, Casper faces Director Hale—the man who blacklisted him, who engineered the original disaster. Hale offers restoration of his name in exchange for the notes' location. Casper realizes his name was never the price; his silence was. Emotional beat: the past confronted, and refused.

chapters.title: Silas Alone
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Believing Casper dead or worse, Silas retrieves the sunken cache with Verity's help and must decide whether to run or fight. She chooses to finish the route herself, guided by everything Casper taught her about reading water. Emotional beat: the student becomes the current that carries the truth.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Amara. The dammed tributary is scheduled to be 'accidentally' released to flood the valley and erase all traces—including witnesses. Amara sabotages the release gate at cost of her own safety, buying hours. Emotional beat: a compromised woman choosing, finally, which side of history to stand on.

chapters.title: Rising Water, Rising Stakes
chapters.summary: POV Casper. As floodwater swamps the detention house, Casper escapes in the chaos with Amara's testimony smuggled to him by a sympathetic guard. He races the crest downriver toward the provincial capital, pursued by Hale's last loyal boat. Emotional beat: desperation sharpened into momentum.

chapters.title: The Race to the Capital
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Silas, running the evidence route independently, and Casper converge at the capital's floodgates—she arrives by the hidden channels, he by the main current, both pursued. Hale corners them on the weir as the flood peaks. Emotional beat: every thread pulled taut; the family reunited at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: Weir
chapters.summary: POV Casper. Climax: on the collapsing weir, Casper chooses surrender over violence, handing the evidence publicly to arriving journalists and inspectors summoned by Verity's network, ensuring Hale cannot bury it with him. Hale is arrested as the water recedes. Emotional beat: victory bought not by force but by refusing to disappear.

chapters.title: Years, Not Miles
chapters.summary: POV Silas. Resolution: months later, cleared of charges, Casper stays in the valley—running a licensed guide service with Silas as his partner-in-navigation and Verity's village as home port. Amara testifies; the dredging is dismantled. Casper finally measures life in years. Emotional beat: belonging earned, invisibility voluntarily ended.
